thread:
maria: Quick design note: proposing checkpointed retry tokens + a bounded 'owner' index at the gateway. Goal: keep resume semantics, limit memory, and improve observability.

ken: TL;DR of the failure modes?

maria: 1) long-lived streams -> OOM, 2) retries spawning duplicate upstream side-effects, 3) poor traceability of who served a resume. Proposal: token = (id, seq, owner_hint). Gateway keeps a memory-first owner-index keyed by token id, spills LRU to disk above N entries.

leo: Is owner_hint trusted?

maria: No. We HMAC server-side assignments; client hints ignored unless verified. Hints only steer sticky routing.

ken: Retry safety & hedging?

maria: Upstream advertises safety with X-Upstream-Op-Safety. Safe retries can reattach to same owner if checkpoint_seq matches. Hedge candidates get ephemeral ids and only the winner is promoted to persisted owner.

devops-bot: alert rule gateway_owner_spill > 0 for 5m created (ops-oncall).

leo: Partial handoff and cancels?

maria: Handoff is: reserve -> send resume -> swap -> emit handoff_complete. If cancel occurs mid-step, send resume_abort to upstream and ack client. Tests for partial ACKs/timeouts required.

ken: Race on simultaneous resumes?

maria: Token-level mutex: first attach wins, others get 409 + Retry-After. Metric resume_conflict_count to track.

leo: SLOs for resume attach?

maria: Target 99p attach <200ms (mem), <1s (disk). Canary in us-west2.

maria: Rollout: emit tokens behind flag -> metrics -> mem-only attach -> enable spill -> canary -> global. Docs + playbook: /playbooks/gateway/checkpointed-retries. Feedback welcome. :rocket:
